## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by brown to reddish-brown forewings with darker angled lines and a wedge-like resting shape that helps it blend into bark, dead leaves, and low vegetation. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, forest edges, lawns, parks, and other open or semi-open habitats where wood sorrels are present. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on Oxalis species, linking common low-growing herbs with the broader food web for birds, spiders, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
